1.why: All nine screens are static, single-column cards with no animation, carousels, or pop-up overlays; only a persistent Logs panel is added below the card.

2.why: Each screen has one large bold heading and a single filled dark-blue primary button, making the key action stand out, though the high-contrast black Logs panel competes visually for attention.

3.why: Each step presents one field and one action so the needed control is immediately visible, but the requirement to hunt for tokens/codes inside the technical Logs panel slows the user.

4.why: The flow requires remembering/carrying a 64-character token, two separate six-digit codes, and a new 14-character password across seven screens with no progress indicator or summary.

5.why: No password manager suggestion, autofill hint, 'remember me' checkbox, show-password toggle, or generate-password option appears on any screen, including the sign-in step.

6.why: There is nothing saved or recognizable presented back to the user—no masked account contact echo, no remembered device, and passwords are shown only as dots.

7.why: Instructional text is one or two short plain-language sentences per screen (e.g., 'Create a new password for your hospital account'), though the raw hex token and log jargon are hard to read.

8.why: No error state is shown in any of the nine screenshots, so there is no evidence that error messages describe a problem and its fix; only static hint text is visible.

9.why: Step 1 gives a concrete format example ('Example: name@example.org or +15551234567'), step 5 states the exact password rules, and code steps point to where the test code is.

10.why: Only password plus emailed token plus six-digit codes exist; there is no face/biometric or passkey option, and the labelled choices are limited rather than clearly presented alternatives.

11.why: Each screen offers at most one input and one primary action (with at most one secondary link), so the user is never overloaded with options.

12.why: Confirmation screens such as 'Privacy statement accepted — your acknowledgement has been securely recorded' and the 'recovery instructions have been prepared' notice state outcomes, though intermediate steps like token verification jump forward without explicit success feedback.

13.why: Short helper hints and a repeated 'Safe authentication' security tip appear on every screen, but there is no help link, contact option, or guidance explaining why extra steps are needed.

14.why: No back link, 'resend code', 'start over', or retry affordance is visible on any screen, so recovering from a mistyped token or code is not demonstrably supported.

15.why: Every step reuses the same header, card layout, bold heading, hint-text style, primary button placement, and green safety notice, giving a highly consistent design.
